subject: Data Engineering
title: Managed Airflow Services
description: A fast breakdown of Managed Airflow Services for builders.

hook.text: Running Airflow yourself means managing a web server, scheduler, database, and worker fleet. Or you let the cloud do it.

buildup.text: MWAA on AWS and Cloud Composer on GCP offer fully managed Apache Airflow environments.

discovery.text: You upload DAG files. The platform handles infrastructure, scaling, logging, and Airflow version upgrades.

twist.text: Managed Airflow is expensive. Small teams may find it cheaper to run Airflow on a single VM.

climax.text: Managed services make sense when your DAG count grows and ops overhead exceeds the service premium.

punchline.text: Pay for managed. Or pay with your time. Choose.

quiz.question: When does managed Airflow make the most financial sense?
options: When DAG count grows and ops overhead exceeds the service cost
For teams with only one simple pipeline
